groups.label: Cross-boundary model variants
groups.basis: Same held-out test split, but variants differ in features or training objective. Ablations share training rows; robustness variants are not controlled experiments.
groups.limitations: Do not treat variant differences as causal unless only the named feature set changed. PR-AUC is bounded and class-imbalanced; prefer absolute differences over percent improvement.

groups.label: Time-ordered folds
groups.basis: Expanding-window folds scored in-domain and on the same held-out test split; the four rows are repeated measurements of one validation design.
groups.limitations: Folds are not independent samples and cover different market periods. Report dispersion, not a single fold as the result.

groups.label: Anomaly detectors
groups.basis: Different algorithms and different sample sizes (LOF uses 5,000 rows; the others 50,000). AUC is computed against fraud labels for evaluation only.
groups.limitations: Sample-size and algorithm differences prevent a clean ranking. LOF's AUC is not directly comparable to the 50,000-row detectors.

groups.label: 2D embeddings
groups.basis: Separability is measured by a logistic classifier on each 2D embedding, with different hyperparameters per embedding.
groups.limitations: Hyperparameters and geometry differ. Use as a qualitative diagnostic, not a model-selection leaderboard.

groups.label: Hour-encoding comparison
groups.basis: The same narrow three-feature model and time-ordered holdout, varying only the hour encoding.
groups.limitations: Only three features plus category; a 0.0003 difference is not material evidence for a general encoding recommendation.

metricNotes.pr_auc: Precision-recall AUC. Sensitive to class prevalence; do not compare across different splits or samples.
metricNotes.roc_auc: ROC AUC. Less sensitive to prevalence but can look strong when the positive class is rare; report alongside PR-AUC.
metricNotes.delta: Absolute difference in the metric's native units (fraction, 0–1), not a percentage improvement.
